title: Credit controller and collector
overviewOfRole: Monitor and manage customer accounts, following financial policies to collect money owed to organisations

knowledges.detail: The principles and functions of credit management or debt collection relevant to the role, how it operates within the organisation, and its interaction with other areas of the organisation.

Standard operating procedures and processes to facilitate the collection of monies owed, for example invoicing, monitoring payments, allocating and reconciling cash, contacting customers to collect debt or outstanding balances, resolving account queries and straightforward disputes, and providing debt support.

Recognised call protocols or frameworks used to understand vulnerability, assess affordability, arrange payment plans, and apply techniques to reach mutually acceptable solutions to credit or debt issues.

The legal and regulatory requirements related to the role and sector, for example consumer duty, late payment of commercial debts (interest), data protection legislation, and anti-money laundering regulations.
Risk management and compliance requirements, including awareness of when escalation is required and the consequences of non-compliance.
Organisational policies and procedures relevant to the credit management or debt collection role.
Professional expectations regarding etiquette, ethics, timeliness, and meeting deadlines, including how to support  vulnerable customers.
The products and or services offered by the organisation, relevant to the role, including their features and benefits.
How the role supports the delivery of products and or services, aligns with organisational strategies and objectives, and contributes to meeting key performance indicators (KPIs).
Principles of effective teamwork and how to work collaboratively with others.
Techniques for managing client relationships and the importance of achieving positive customer outcomes.
Communication methods, including verbal, non-verbal, written, and digital, and how to adapt these to different audiences to ensure information is communicated effectively.
The systems, tools, and processes used in the role, including IT systems and emerging technologies.
Awareness of cybersecurity risks and how to stay safe and secure online, including data protection requirements and the secure handling of data.
Reporting procedures and understanding when and how to raise concerns or issues, including the consequences of not following procedures.
How professional standards can be used to improve own working practices, and techniques to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
Awareness of relevant current and emerging sustainability principles and how to apply these within the role.
Awareness of organisational equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) policies.

behaviours.detail: Demonstrates resilience in adapting to change and in challenging situations.
Demonstrates a collaborative mindset and is supportive of others when setbacks occur.
Acts with integrity and applies an ethical approach when dealing with others.
Is committed to continuing professional development (CPD) to maintain and enhance competence in their own area of practice, and to keep up to date with legal, regulatory, and technological changes.
Is resolute in taking responsibility for achieving goals.

skills.detail: Meet key performance indicators (KPIs) in line with organisational, legal, and regulatory requirements.
Process, record, and monitor customer accounts within own work remit.
Facilitate the collection of monies owed by following standard operating procedures, escalating issues where required.
Use recognised call protocols or frameworks to assess affordability, arrange payment plans, and use techniques to reach mutually acceptable solutions to credit or debt issues.

Follow legal, regulatory, and organisational policies and procedures relevant to the credit management and or debt collection role, for example recognising and managing customer vulnerability and customers in financial difficulty.
Build positive relationships with colleagues and customers.

Communicate with customers and colleagues using a range of media, such as email, telephone, and online communications, adapting communication style to suit the audience, for example vulnerable customers.

Use standard systems and processes to meet business and customer needs, for example IT systems and tools, Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, use of AI, and automated workflows where applicable.

Use digital technology and data analytics safely and securely in day-to-day activities and in line with data protection requirements, for example sharing information in compliance with data protection legislation and organisational policy.
Report or escalate issues where appropriate, in line with organisational procedures and legal and regulatory requirements.
Identify opportunities to improve own working practices and implement changes to improve performance.
Organise workload to complete tasks and meet deadlines, taking ownership of work through to resolution and problem-solving issues where appropriate.

clusterDescription: Provide highly accurate support to operations and administration across wide areas of financial service areas including research and analysis compliant with relevant regulations. Deliver support to clients and to client account management (risk, collection, enforcement, recovery)

duties.dutyDetail: Engage with customers in a positive way to understand their circumstances, to ensure payment on time, and, where relevant, use recognised call frameworks to understand vulnerabilities, assess affordability, and determine the ability to pay.
Facilitate the collection of monies owed from business or individual customers by arranging payments or payment plans, or identifying vulnerability and signposting advice.
Work with customers to identify mutually acceptable solutions to credit and or debt issues, taking ownership through to resolution and escalating where necessary.

Manage credit or debt risks and make decisions, seeking guidance from line managers or escalating where appropriate, for example about queries, complaints, or vulnerability, in line with organisational policies and procedures.
Achieve credit management or debt recovery key performance indicators (KPIs) in line with organisational, legal, and regulatory requirements.
Organise own workload to achieve work objectives, completing tasks to required deadlines.
Use systems, tools, and standard processes to track, monitor, record, and process credit and or debt collection cases.
Contribute to team improvement, and interact and cooperate effectively within the team.
Keep up to date with, and adhere to, relevant regulatory, legal, and policy changes.
Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying and suggesting opportunities to improve own working practices, and implementing required changes.
